landing.headline:
Your team’s scattered records,
gathered into
one feature map
landing.lede: LinkBoard groups the work, decisions, and designs scattered across GitHub, Notion, and Figma into a single map, feature by feature.

sources.github: Why the code → the map’s backbone

problem.title:
The records are still there.
The context is not.

items.1: Code lives in GitHub, decisions in Notion, screen intent in Figma. Understanding one feature means switching windows three times.
items.2: Only the people who were there know that “this PR came out of that meeting.”
items.3: “Two reviewers, no Friday deploys” — rules nobody wrote down, yet everybody follows.

1.title: A map grouped by feature
1.desc:
People don’t think in sources. They think in “the checkout feature.”
Designs, decisions, and code for one feature gather on a single branch.

2.title: Answers that cite their source
2.desc:
Answers come from your team’s actual records, with links to the originals.
No source, no answer.
2.question: Q) Why is coupon support on hold?

3.title: Team norms, confirmed by the lead
3.desc:
Undocumented norms are inferred from PR and review patterns and proposed as candidates.
Only what the lead confirms becomes visible to the team.

cta.title:
“Why is it like this?”
Now the map answers.
cta.desc: The lead connects the sources once. Everyone who joins after that never has to ask.
